boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Texas Tech University
boards.description: Ten currently documented late-hours food stops in Lubbock, including several along the University Avenue and 4th Street approaches to Texas Tech.

cards.title: Whataburger at 9th & University
cards.subtitle: 2412 9th St, Lubbock
cards.notes: Use the dining room for a late meal at the 9th-and-University location. Check the official page before leaving, since holiday operations can differ.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour dining-room option on the University Avenue approach to campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Whataburger lists its dine-in service at 2412 9th St as 24 hours daily.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists dine-in as 24 hours every day; drive-thru is listed closed. Holiday hours may differ.

cards.title: IHOP at 1627 University Ave
cards.subtitle: 1627 University Ave, Lubbock
cards.notes: Plan for a sit-down or takeout stop near 19th Street and University Avenue. The location page lists round-the-clock restaurant hours.
cards.short_summary: An all-hours pancake and breakfast stop on University Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: IHOP lists the restaurant at 1627 University Ave as open 24 hours Monday through Sunday.
cards.source_title: IHOP Breakfast Restaurants Near You at 1627 University Ave
cards.access_notes: Official page lists restaurant hours as open 24 hours every day and identifies dine-in and takeout amenities.

cards.title: Denny's at 4718 Slide Rd
cards.subtitle: 4718 Slide Rd, Lubbock
cards.notes: Head to Slide Road when you want a full diner menu after normal dinner hours. The official location page says the restaurant is open around the clock.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour diner option with breakfast, lunch, and dinner service.
cards.evidence_claim: Denny's lists its restaurant at 4718 Slide Rd as open 24 hours.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists the restaurant as open 24 hours daily and offers online ordering and walk-ins.

cards.title: Raising Cane's on 4th Street
cards.subtitle: 5702 4th St, Lubbock
cards.notes: Take 4th Street west from the Texas Tech area for dine-in, drive-thru, or curbside service. Confirm the posted hours if visiting around a holiday.
cards.short_summary: A 4th Street chicken-finger restaurant serving until 3 a.m. daily.
cards.evidence_claim: Raising Cane's lists both dine-in and drive-thru hours at 5702 4th Street as 10 a.m. to 3 a.m. every day.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists dine-in and drive-thru service until 3 a.m. Sunday through Saturday; curbside pickup is available.

cards.title: Raising Cane's on 82nd Street
cards.subtitle: 2725 82nd St, Lubbock
cards.notes: Use this south-Lubbock location when the 4th Street route is not convenient. Its official page separately posts dine-in and drive-thru closing times.
cards.short_summary: A Cane's location with 2 a.m. closes most nights and 3 a.m. weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: Raising Cane's lists 2725 82nd Street open until 2 a.m. Sunday through Thursday and 3 a.m. Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists dine-in and drive-thru until 2 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 3 a.m. Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Taco Bell at 402 Ave Q
cards.subtitle: 402 Ave Q, Lubbock
cards.notes: Use the drive-thru for the late window at this central-Lubbock Taco Bell. Dine-in is listed separately, so rely on the drive-thru schedule after evening hours.
cards.short_summary: A drive-thru option posted until 2 a.m. most nights and 3 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-thru hours at 402 Ave Q until 2 a.m. Sunday through Thursday and 3 a.m. Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell at 402 Ave Q, Lubbock
cards.access_notes: Official page lists drive-thru hours until 2 a.m. most nights and 3 a.m. Friday–Saturday; dine-in is listed closed.

cards.title: Taco Bell at 5713 Fourth Street
cards.subtitle: 5713 Fourth St, Lubbock
cards.notes: Keep this 4th Street drive-thru in mind for an after-hours order west of campus. The official locator identifies this specific Lubbock restaurant as open late.
cards.short_summary: A 4th Street Taco Bell whose official locator lists late-night drive-thru availability.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell's official Lubbock locator lists the restaurant at 5713 Fourth Street as open until 2 a.m.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell at 5713 Fourth Street, Lubbock
cards.access_notes: Official Taco Bell locator lists the 5713 Fourth Street location as open until 2 a.m.; verify the day-specific drive-thru schedule before travel.

cards.title: Taco Bell at 5010 Milwaukee Ave
cards.subtitle: 5010 Milwaukee Ave, Lubbock
cards.notes: For a west-Lubbock drive-thru stop, use the posted late schedule at Milwaukee Avenue. The dining room closes earlier than the drive-thru.
cards.short_summary: A Milwaukee Avenue drive-thru serving until 1 a.m. weekdays and 2 a.m. weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-thru hours at 5010 Milwaukee Ave until 1 a.m. Sunday through Thursday and 2 a.m. Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell Takeout at 5010 Milwaukee Ave, Lubbock
cards.access_notes: Official page lists drive-thru service until 1 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 2 a.m. Friday–Saturday; dine-in closes earlier.

cards.title: McDonald's at 6501 4th Street
cards.subtitle: 6501 4th St, Lubbock
cards.notes: This 4th Street restaurant is another documented all-hours food stop west of Texas Tech. Use the restaurant entrance rather than assuming drive-thru hours match.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour McDonald's restaurant on the westbound 4th Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: McDonald's lists restaurant and lobby hours at 6501 4th Street as open 24 hours every day.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists the restaurant and lobby as open 24 hours daily; it separately lists drive-thru hours ending at 1 a.m.

cards.title: Subway at 1109 University Ave
cards.subtitle: 1109 University Ave, Lubbock
cards.notes: Choose the University Avenue Subway when you need a sandwich close to the campus approach. Confirm the exact storefront details with the official locator before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A University Avenue Subway listed as open 24 hours in the official Lubbock locator.
cards.evidence_claim: Subway's official Lubbock location directory lists the restaurant at 1109 University Ave as open 24 hours every day.
cards.access_notes: Official Lubbock directory lists 1109 University Ave as open 24 hours daily; use the locator to confirm current store details.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Texas Tech spaces for studying, campus programs, recreation, and public cultural stops.

cards.title: Student Union Building
cards.subtitle: 2625 15th Street, Texas Tech campus
cards.notes: Use the building as a central meet-up point before campus events, then check its posted services, room options, and building hours.
cards.short_summary: Texas Tech’s campus community center combines events, services, and student spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech describes the Student Union Building as a home for the campus to come together for events, educational opportunities, and services.
cards.access_notes: Check the Student Union site for current building hours and room-access details.

cards.title: Escondido Theatre
cards.subtitle: Student Union Building, Room 001
cards.notes: Look for Student Activities Board programs here, or reserve it through the SUB process when planning an eligible organization event.
cards.short_summary: A 100-seat SUB-basement theatre used for organized campus programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech lists Escondido Theatre as SUB room 001 with a maximum capacity of 100, and its Student Government Association schedules training there.
cards.access_notes: Programming and reservations are managed by the Student Union; availability varies by event.

cards.title: Study Room 2W5
cards.subtitle: University Library, Stacks 2
cards.notes: Reserve this four-person study room when a small group needs a shared screen, outlets, and a defined place to work together.
cards.short_summary: A reservable library group room with a smartboard and power.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech Libraries lists Study Room 2W5 as a four-person study space with three outlets, one smartboard, and power available.
cards.source_title: Study Room 2W5 | Texas Tech University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Use the Libraries’ room-reservation calendar to see availability and booking rules.

cards.entity_name: Robert H. Ewalt Student Rec Center
cards.title: Robert H. Ewalt Student Rec Center
cards.subtitle: 3219 A Main Street, Texas Tech campus
cards.notes: Meet for a court sport, climbing, fitness, or other recreation after confirming member access and the day’s facility schedule.
cards.short_summary: The main recreation facility brings several indoor activity options into one building.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech’s membership page lists indoor fitness space, group fitness classes, and a 53-foot indoor climbing wall among Recreation membership access.
cards.access_notes: Students who paid the University Recreation fee may use facilities for their enrolled semester; others may need membership.

cards.title: Leisure Pool
cards.subtitle: Recreational Aquatic Facilities, 3219 Main Street
cards.notes: Plan a swim or lazy-river visit with friends after checking the daily aquatics schedule and confirming your Recreation access.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor recreation pool with lap swimming, a water slide, and a lazy river.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech lists the Leisure Pool as featuring a 645-foot lazy river, lap swimming, and a water slide.
cards.access_notes: Entry requires a valid TTU ID or membership; pool operations and hours change by schedule.

cards.title: Indoor Climbing Center
cards.subtitle: Robert H. Ewalt Student Rec Center
cards.notes: Bring a partner for a climbing session, and check the Recreation schedule for open hours and any required orientation details.
cards.short_summary: A 53-foot climbing wall inside Texas Tech’s recreation facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech’s Recreation membership information includes an Indoor Climbing Center with a 53-foot-tall rock wall.
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to Recreation facility access and the current climbing-center schedule.

cards.title: Urbanovsky Park
cards.subtitle: 1500 Flint Avenue, Texas Tech campus
cards.notes: Choose a court, the running trail, or disc-golf course for a low-key outdoor activity, then verify access through Recreation.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation park with courts, fields, trail, and disc golf.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech lists Urbanovsky Park among its athletics and recreation locations at 1500 Flint Avenue.
cards.source_title: Athletics & Recreation | Campus Locations | Texas Tech
cards.access_notes: Recreation facilities are primarily intended for student recreational and instructional use; follow posted park and facility rules.

cards.title: International Cultural Center
cards.subtitle: 601 Indiana Avenue, Texas Tech campus
cards.notes: Use the globe outside as an easy landmark, then attend a listed cultural program or arrange an eligible meeting through campus procedures.
cards.short_summary: A campus cultural-events facility marked by a large globe sculpture.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech’s directions identify the International Cultural Center at 601 Indiana Avenue and note the large globe sculpture in front.
cards.source_title: Directions to the International Cultural Center | Texas Tech
cards.access_notes: Specific rooms and areas are scheduled through International Affairs; attend public programming or reserve through the applicable process.

cards.title: Museum of Texas Tech University
cards.subtitle: 3301 4th Street, Lubbock
cards.notes: Build in time for the galleries as a study-break destination, and confirm exhibition details before heading over with classmates or visitors.
cards.short_summary: A university museum offering public cultural programming near the campus core.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech’s International Student Life page identifies the Texas Tech Museum at 3301 4th Street and states that admission is free.
cards.source_title: Global Techsan Welcome Days | Texas Tech
cards.access_notes: Verify current museum gallery hours and exhibition availability before visiting.

cards.title: National Ranching Heritage Center
cards.subtitle: 3121 4th Street, Lubbock
cards.notes: Walk the historic-preservation site with a friend or visiting family, using the center’s current visitor information to plan the stop.
cards.short_summary: A named Texas Tech heritage destination beside the museum district.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech’s International Student Life page identifies the National Ranching Heritage Center at 3121 4th Street and states that admission is free.
cards.source_title: Global Techsan Welcome Days | Texas Tech
cards.access_notes: Verify current visitor hours, routes, and any program-specific arrangements before visiting.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission places for a shared walk, gallery browse, or conversation around Texas Tech and Lubbock.

cards.entity_name: A Changing World: Dinosaurs, Diversity, and Drifting Continents Gallery
cards.title: Trace Texas’s prehistoric past
cards.subtitle: Museum of Texas Tech University
cards.notes: Meet at the museum and move through the Mesozoic-era displays together; keep the conversation going with a favorite fossil or landscape detail.
cards.short_summary: A free museum gallery focused on Texas during the Mesozoic Era.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum identifies A Changing World as a long-term gallery about Texas during the Mesozoic Era, and museum admission is free every day.
cards.access_notes: Visit during museum hours; the museum lists Tuesday–Saturday and Sunday hours and asks visitors to check in at the front desk.

cards.title: Compare the Llano’s habitats
cards.subtitle: Museum of Texas Tech University
cards.notes: Walk the habitat displays with a friend and pick one local plant or animal to look for on a later campus stroll; admission does not require a purchase.
cards.short_summary: A free gallery look at biodiversity and seven Llano Estacado habitats.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum’s long-term-exhibitions page describes Biodiversity of the Llano Estacado and its seven major habitats; museum admission is free every day.
cards.access_notes: Enter through the Museum of Texas Tech University during posted museum hours and check in at the front desk.

cards.title: Browse Western American art
cards.subtitle: Museum of Texas Tech University
cards.notes: Use the paintings, drawings, and sculptures as a low-key prompt for conversation; pause on one work each and share what caught your attention.
cards.short_summary: A free museum stop featuring Western American art from the Diamond M Collection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum lists the Diamond M Collection among its long-term exhibitions and describes 380 American artworks; museum admission is free every day.
cards.access_notes: The collection is inside the Museum of Texas Tech University; use the museum’s posted hours and front-desk check-in.

cards.entity_name: Ice Age on the Southern Plains
cards.title: See Ice Age megafauna
cards.subtitle: Museum of Texas Tech University
cards.notes: Take a shared lap through the mounted skeletons and murals, then compare which prehistoric animal feels most surprising in the Southern Plains setting.
cards.short_summary: A free gallery with regional Pleistocene animals and landscape interpretation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum describes Ice Age on the Southern Plains as a long-term gallery with Pleistocene megafauna, mounted skeletons, and murals; admission is free every day.
cards.access_notes: Inside the Museum of Texas Tech University; arrive during posted museum hours and check in at the front desk.

cards.title: Talk through Southwest art
cards.subtitle: Museum of Texas Tech University
cards.notes: Choose a few works from the Southwestern art displays and trade observations; the gallery is an easy indoor stop with no admission purchase required.
cards.short_summary: A free museum gallery of 20th- and 21st-century Southwestern art.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum describes the Talkington Gallery of Art as featuring 20th- and 21st-century art of the Southwestern United States; museum admission is free every day.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Museum of Texas Tech University; follow posted museum hours and front-desk check-in guidance.

cards.entity_name: William C. and Evelyn M. Davies Gallery of Southwest Indian Art
cards.title: Study Southwest Indian art
cards.subtitle: Museum of Texas Tech University
cards.notes: Browse ceramics, textiles, carvings, basketry, and mixed media at your own pace; use the object labels to guide a respectful shared discussion.
cards.short_summary: A free gallery presenting art and handicraft from more than 20 Native American tribes.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum states that the Davies Gallery displays art and handicraft representing more than 20 Native American tribes; museum admission is free every day.
cards.access_notes: Inside the Museum of Texas Tech University; visit during posted museum hours and check in at the front desk.

cards.entity_name: Nature Trail at Lubbock Lake Landmark
cards.title: Walk the nature trail
cards.subtitle: Lubbock Lake Landmark, Lubbock
cards.notes: Sign in at the Nash Interpretive Center, then take the nature trail together and use the interpretive signs to identify plants, animals, and archaeology.
cards.short_summary: A free, signposted trail through native mixed-grass plains habitat.
cards.evidence_claim: Lubbock Lake Landmark lists a 2.5–3.5-mile nature trail and states that admission to the Interpretive Center and trails is free.
cards.source_title: Hiking Trails | Lubbock Lake Landmark | Texas Tech
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday 9 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sunday 1–5 p.m.; sign in first and leave the premises by 5 p.m. Trails close with the center.

cards.entity_name: Wildflower Trail at Lubbock Lake Landmark
cards.title: Take a wildflower walk
cards.subtitle: Lubbock Lake Landmark, Lubbock
cards.notes: Meet at the interpretive center and follow the short trail’s plant-identification signs; bring water and make time to stop rather than rush the loop.
cards.short_summary: A free half-mile trail identifying native plants, trees, and wildflowers.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech describes the Wildflower Trail at Lubbock Lake Landmark as a 0.5-mile trail identifying native plants, trees, and wildflowers; admission is free.
cards.source_title: Hiking Trails | Lubbock Lake Landmark | Texas Tech
cards.access_notes: Open only while the Interpretive Center is open: Tuesday–Saturday 9 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sunday 1–5 p.m.; sign in before heading out.

cards.entity_name: Archaeological Trail at Lubbock Lake Landmark
cards.title: Follow 12,000 years of history
cards.subtitle: Lubbock Lake Landmark, Lubbock
cards.notes: Start after signing in and read the trail interpretation together; stay on designated paths and plan to be off the grounds before the listed closing time.
cards.short_summary: A free half-mile archaeology-focused trail at the Landmark preserve.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech describes Lubbock Lake Landmark’s 0.5-mile Archaeological Trail and states that admission to its Interpretive Center and trails is free.
cards.source_title: Hiking Trails | Lubbock Lake Landmark | Texas Tech
cards.access_notes: Sign in at the Nash Interpretive Center; trails are open Tuesday–Saturday 9 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sunday 1–5 p.m., and are closed after hours.

cards.title: See an international art exhibit
cards.subtitle: International Cultural Center, Texas Tech University
cards.notes: Drop in with a friend to view the current gallery exhibition, then use a single photograph or artwork as a conversation starter before heading back across campus.
cards.short_summary: Free, public international-themed exhibitions in the International Cultural Center galleries.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech International Affairs states that all International Cultural Center exhibits and receptions are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: The page identifies current and upcoming exhibits; check the exhibit listing before going because individual displays can change.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct University Library settings, from quiet stacks and reservable rooms to technology-equipped group areas.

cards.title: Study Hub
cards.subtitle: University Library ground floor
cards.notes: Bring a group project here for conference tables, semi-private seating, whiteboard walls, and display-based screen sharing.
cards.short_summary: A ground-floor collaboration area with whiteboards and wireless display sharing.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech Libraries describes the Study Hub as a ground-floor group-study area with conference tables, semi-private spaces, whiteboard walls, and HD displays for sharing screens.
cards.source_title: Ground Floor Group Study | University Libraries | Texas Tech
cards.access_notes: Located in the University Library; use TTUnet and the displayed connection address for the listed wireless screen-sharing workflow.

cards.title: Research Hub (Room 132)
cards.subtitle: University Library first floor
cards.notes: Set up here when your work may benefit from nearby one-on-one librarian assistance as well as an open study setting.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor study space paired with access to individual librarian help.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech Libraries identifies the Research Hub in Room 132 as study space with one-on-one assistance from librarians.
cards.source_title: Looking for study space? | News at the Libraries | Texas Tech
cards.access_notes: Room 132 is on the University Library's first floor; confirm building access before a visit.

cards.title: University Library Mezzanine
cards.subtitle: University Library mezzanine level
cards.notes: Choose this level for individual or group work near public computers and the library's personal-librarian services.
cards.short_summary: A non-quiet mezzanine with individual and group seating plus public computers.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech Libraries designates the mezzanine as a non-quiet floor with individual and group study spaces and public computers.
cards.source_title: Looking for study space? | News at the Libraries | Texas Tech
cards.access_notes: The library lists the mezzanine as a non-quiet area; plan accordingly for collaboration rather than silence.

cards.title: University Library Basement
cards.subtitle: University Library basement level
cards.notes: Use the basement when you need a non-quiet library floor with both individual and group study options.
cards.short_summary: A basement-level option for individual or collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech Libraries designates the University Library basement as a non-quiet floor with individual and group study spaces.
cards.source_title: Looking for study space? | News at the Libraries | Texas Tech
cards.access_notes: The basement is listed as non-quiet; confirm University Library building access before visiting.

cards.title: Dynamic Media Services
cards.subtitle: University Library second floor east
cards.notes: Head to second-floor east if a Mac computer lab would help with your work alongside individual or group seating.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor-east study area with access to the library's Mac computer lab.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech Libraries lists Dynamic Media Services on the second floor east as a non-quiet area with individual and group study spaces and a Mac computer lab.
cards.source_title: Looking for study space? | News at the Libraries | Texas Tech
cards.access_notes: Dynamic Media Services is on the University Library's second-floor east side and is designated non-quiet.

cards.title: University Library Stacks 1
cards.subtitle: University Library quiet-study stacks
cards.notes: Reserve an individual study carrel through the library's Study Spaces site when you want a quiet stacks-level setting.
cards.short_summary: A quiet stacks level with reservable individual study carrels.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech Libraries designates Stacks 1–5 as quiet study areas and states that individual study carrels can be reserved through its Study Spaces site.
cards.source_title: Looking for study space? | News at the Libraries | Texas Tech
cards.access_notes: Stacks 1 is a designated quiet-study area; individual carrels require reservation through the library's Study Spaces process.

cards.entity_name: University Library Stacks 2 Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Stacks 2 Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: University Library quiet-study stacks
cards.notes: Use a closed group study room on this quiet stacks level when your group needs a more contained work session.
cards.short_summary: Closed group rooms within a designated quiet-study stacks level.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech Libraries designates Stacks 1–5 as quiet study areas and identifies closed-off group study rooms on Stacks 2, 4, and 5.
cards.source_title: Looking for study space? | News at the Libraries | Texas Tech
cards.access_notes: Stacks 2 is designated quiet study; the library identifies closed-off group rooms on this level.

cards.title: University Library Stacks 3
cards.subtitle: University Library quiet-study stacks
cards.notes: Use this designated quiet-study stacks level for focused reading, writing, or solo review, and keep conversations elsewhere.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet-study level in the University Library stacks.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech Libraries designates Stacks 1–5, including Stacks 3, as quiet study areas.
cards.source_title: Looking for study space? | News at the Libraries | Texas Tech
cards.access_notes: Stacks 3 is designated for quiet study; confirm University Library building access before visiting.

cards.entity_name: University Library Stacks 4 Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Stacks 4 Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: University Library quiet-study stacks
cards.notes: Plan a contained group session in a closed room on Stacks 4, while respecting the library's quiet-study designation.
cards.short_summary: Closed group rooms on a library level designated for quiet study.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech Libraries designates Stacks 1–5 as quiet study areas and identifies closed-off group study rooms on Stacks 2, 4, and 5.
cards.source_title: Looking for study space? | News at the Libraries | Texas Tech
cards.access_notes: Stacks 4 is a quiet-study level with closed-off group study rooms identified by the library.

cards.entity_name: University Library Stacks 5 Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Stacks 5 Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: University Library quiet-study stacks
cards.notes: Choose a closed group room on Stacks 5 for a contained session, then preserve the quiet character of the level.
cards.short_summary: Closed group rooms on the fifth quiet-study stacks level.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech Libraries designates Stacks 1–5 as quiet study areas and identifies closed-off group study rooms on Stacks 2, 4, and 5.
cards.source_title: Looking for study space? | News at the Libraries | Texas Tech
cards.access_notes: Stacks 5 is a quiet-study level with closed-off group study rooms identified by the library.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along the 19th Street corridor beside or within the practical orbit of Texas Tech University.

cards.title: Skyviews Restaurant
cards.subtitle: 19th Street and University Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Reserve a table at the Texas Tech Plaza building’s top-floor teaching restaurant, located at the southeast corner of 19th and University.
cards.short_summary: A campus-adjacent restaurant operated through Texas Tech’s hospitality program.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech identifies Skyviews as a top-floor restaurant at 1901 University Avenue, on the southeast corner of University Avenue and 19th Street adjacent to campus.
cards.access_notes: Lunch service is listed for fall and spring semesters when classes are in session; dinner events require reservations.

cards.title: Buddy Holly Center
cards.subtitle: 19th Street and Crickets Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Visit the historic depot at 1801 Crickets Avenue to see exhibits about Buddy Holly, West Texas music, and contemporary visual art.
cards.short_summary: A City of Lubbock cultural center in a renovated historic depot.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Lubbock says the Buddy Holly Center preserves and interprets Buddy Holly and West Texas music artifacts and presents contemporary visual-art exhibitions.
cards.source_title: Buddy Holly Center | City of Lubbock
cards.access_notes: The City lists the Center at 1801 Crickets Avenue, at the northeast corner of 19th Street and Crickets Avenue.

cards.entity_name: Buddy and Maria Elena Holly Plaza
cards.title: Buddy and Maria Elena Holly Plaza
cards.subtitle: 19th Street and Crickets Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Walk the plaza west of the Buddy Holly Center to view the West Texas Walk of Fame and Grant Speed’s Buddy Holly statue.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor public plaza with a documented music-history landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Lubbock places the West Texas Walk of Fame and Buddy Holly statue inside this plaza at Crickets Avenue and 19th Street.
cards.source_title: Buddy Holly Center | City of Lubbock
cards.access_notes: The City states that the plaza is open to the public from dawn to dusk year round.

cards.title: Cast Iron Grill
cards.subtitle: 19th Street corridor near Avenue K
cards.notes: Plan a daytime stop at 620 19th Street for the restaurant’s listed breakfast service or lunch service before the 2 p.m. close.
cards.short_summary: A daytime dining stop directly on 19th Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Cast Iron Grill lists its address as 620 19th Street and states that it serves breakfast Monday through Friday from 7 a.m. and lunch until 2 p.m.
cards.access_notes: The business lists weekday breakfast from 7 a.m. to about 10:30 a.m. and lunch until 2 p.m.

cards.title: McDonald's at 2339 19th Street
cards.subtitle: 19th Street corridor near University Avenue
cards.notes: Use the official restaurant locator to confirm this named 19th Street location when you need a straightforward meal stop near campus.
cards.short_summary: A directly listed restaurant location on the campus-edge corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: McDonald’s official Lubbock restaurant directory lists a location at 2339 19th Street.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current service details through the official locator before leaving.

cards.title: Café J
cards.subtitle: 19th Street corridor near University Avenue
cards.notes: Choose from the restaurant’s published brunch, lunch, or dinner menus at its 2605 19th Street address; reserve ahead if desired.
cards.short_summary: A menu-based restaurant stop a short way west of the campus edge.
cards.evidence_claim: Café J’s official site lists its Lubbock address as 2605 19th Street and publishes brunch, lunch, and dinner menus.
cards.access_notes: The official site lists dining hours and a reservation link; check them before visiting.

cards.title: Schlotzsky's Deli 19th St
cards.subtitle: 19th Street corridor near Quaker Avenue
cards.notes: Stop at the official 3715 19th Street location for the listed sandwiches, pizzas, flatbreads, and salads menu categories.
cards.short_summary: A direct-chain location with its address, offerings, and hours published online.
cards.evidence_claim: Schlotzsky’s identifies its 19th Street location at 3715 19th Street and lists sandwiches, pizzas, flatbreads, and salads.
cards.access_notes: The official location page lists daily hours of 10:30 a.m. to 9 p.m.

cards.title: DoubleDave's Pizzaworks – Lubbock 19th St.
cards.subtitle: 19th Street corridor near Quaker Avenue
cards.notes: Order or dine in at the official 4206 19th Street location, which publishes its daily hours and a location-specific menu link.
cards.short_summary: A pizza restaurant with an official page dedicated to its 19th Street location.
cards.evidence_claim: DoubleDave’s lists its Lubbock 19th Street location at 4206 19th Street, Suite 400, with daily 11 a.m.–10 p.m. hours.
cards.access_notes: The official location page lists daily hours from 11 a.m. to 10 p.m.

cards.title: Market Street at 19th & Quaker
cards.subtitle: 19th Street corridor at Quaker Avenue
cards.notes: Use this 4425 19th Street grocery stop for in-store shopping or the store’s published DriveUp & Go pickup option at 19th and Quaker.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour grocery destination directly on the western 19th Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Market Street’s official page lists the 4425 19th Street store near 19th Street and Quaker Avenue and says it is open 24 hours.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists the grocery store as open 24 hours daily; pharmacy hours differ.

cards.title: Bigham's Smokehouse – 19th Street & Quaker
cards.subtitle: 19th Street corridor at Quaker Avenue
cards.notes: Visit the 4302 19th Street restaurant for a sit-down, carry-out, drive-thru, or delivery barbecue meal using its official location information.
cards.short_summary: A named barbecue restaurant on the 19th Street and Quaker block.
cards.evidence_claim: Bigham’s official site lists its 19th Street location at 4302 19th Street and states that its Lubbock locations offer dine-in, carry-out, drive-thru, or delivery.
cards.access_notes: The official site lists 11 a.m.–8 p.m. Sunday and Tuesday–Thursday, and 11 a.m.–9 p.m. Friday–Saturday.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Texas Tech traditions, from game-day signals and mascots to campus bells, songs, and the annual lighting ceremony.

cards.title: Guns Up
cards.subtitle: The Red Raider greeting and victory sign
cards.notes: Use the hand sign as a greeting or during athletics, following the university’s described finger-and-thumb formation.
cards.short_summary: A Red Raider hand sign adopted as a campus tradition in 1971.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech identifies Guns Up as the widely recognized Red Raider greeting and a victory sign used at athletic events; it says the tradition began in 1971.
cards.access_notes: A gesture used at events and as a greeting; no special access is required to make it.

cards.title: The Masked Rider’s home-game run
cards.subtitle: Mounted mascot entrance at Texas Tech home games
cards.notes: Arrive before kickoff to watch the masked student rider, in cape and mask, lead the team onto the field.
cards.short_summary: Texas Tech’s official mounted mascot has led the team onto the field since 1954.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech states that the Masked Rider became an official mascot in 1954 and today leads the team onto the field for home games.
cards.access_notes: Watch from an authorized game-day seat or event viewing area; athletic-event admission may apply.

cards.title: Raider Red appearances
cards.subtitle: Texas Tech’s costumed public-relations mascot
cards.notes: Look for the costumed mascot at a listed athletics event or campus appearance, and keep interactions respectful.
cards.short_summary: A costumed mascot created in 1971 as an alternative to the mounted Masked Rider.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech says Saddle Tramp Jim Gaspard created Raider Red from a Dirk West drawing as an alternative to the Masked Rider.
cards.access_notes: Appearance locations vary by event; athletic-event admission may apply.

cards.title: Sing the Matador Song
cards.subtitle: Texas Tech’s alma mater
cards.notes: Learn the alma mater before a formal university occasion or athletics event so you can join the song appropriately.
cards.short_summary: The university’s alma mater pairs words by R.C. Marshall with music by Harry Lemaire.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech identifies the Matador Song as its alma mater, with music by Harry Lemaire and words by R.C. Marshall.
cards.access_notes: The lyrics are publicly available on the university traditions page.

cards.title: “Fight, Raiders, Fight!”
cards.subtitle: The Texas Tech fight song
cards.notes: Follow the printed lyrics at a sporting event and listen for the final line that calls out the Victory Bells.
cards.short_summary: Carroll McMath wrote the fight song that names the scarlet and black and Victory Bells.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech credits Carroll McMath with its Fight Song and publishes its lyrics, including the reference to the Victory Bells.
cards.access_notes: The lyrics are publicly available; attendance costs depend on the particular sporting event.

cards.title: Carol of Lights® switch-on
cards.subtitle: Annual holiday ceremony in the Science Quadrangle
cards.notes: Check the campus-events page before attending; the ceremony includes music and the campus-lighting moment in the Science Quadrangle.
cards.short_summary: An annual December lighting ceremony that illuminates campus buildings for the holiday season.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech’s 2026 event page lists Carol of Lights® for December 6 in the Science Quadrangle and says more than 30,000 lights illuminate campus.
cards.source_title: The 67th Annual Carol of Lights | Campus Events | Texas Tech
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for December 6, 2026, with a 6:30 p.m. carillon concert and 7 p.m. ceremony; confirm details before going.

cards.title: Bangin’ Bertha
cards.subtitle: The Saddle Tramps’ trailer-mounted bell
cards.notes: Spot the named bell at a home football game or homecoming event; leave ringing it to the Saddle Tramps.
cards.short_summary: A 1959 bell, designed by a Saddle Tramp and donated by the Santa Fe Railroad.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech says Saddle Tramps carry Bangin’ Bertha to home football games and homecoming events; the bell was designed in 1959 by Joe Winegar.
cards.source_title: Bangin' Bertha (Saddle Tramp Bell) | History & Traditions | TTU
cards.access_notes: Appears at home football games and homecoming events; event admission or access rules may apply.

cards.title: Victory Bells
cards.subtitle: Administration Building east tower
cards.notes: Listen after a Texas Tech victory or special occasion; the university assigns bell-ringing to the Saddle Tramps.
cards.short_summary: Two bells, given as the Class of 1936 gift, mark victories and special occasions.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech says Saddle Tramps ring the Victory Bells after victories and special occasions; the 1,200-pound pair hangs in the Administration Building’s east tower.
cards.access_notes: The bells are university-managed and not for public operation; observe from public campus areas.

cards.title: Old Will wrapped in red
cards.subtitle: Saddle Tramp ritual before home football games
cards.notes: View the Will Rogers and Soapsuds statue near Memorial Circle before a home game; do not touch or add material to it.
cards.short_summary: Saddle Tramps wrap the campus statue in red crepe paper before every home football game.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech states that Saddle Tramps wrap the Will Rogers and Soapsuds statue with red crepe paper before every home football game.
cards.source_title: Will Rogers & Soapsuds | History & Traditions | TTU
cards.access_notes: View the outdoor landmark from public walkways; do not climb, touch, or alter the statue.

cards.title: The pre-kickoff Bell Circle
cards.subtitle: Saddle Tramps’ football kickoff formation
cards.notes: Be in the stadium before kickoff to see the Saddle Tramps form the Bell Circle; follow venue and staff directions.
cards.short_summary: A Saddle Tramp pre-kickoff ritual documented by the university alongside bell ringing and campus-event service.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech describes the Saddle Tramps as forming the “Bell Circle” moments before football kickoff, alongside their other tradition-keeping roles.
cards.access_notes: Visible during football pregame from authorized stadium seating; game admission may apply.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Texas Tech University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure first-weekend loop: get oriented, find campus resources, spend time outdoors, and add a few photo-ready Texas Tech landmarks.

cards.title: Start at Memorial Circle
cards.subtitle: First look at a focal point of campus
cards.notes: Begin with a slow walk around the circle and Pfluger Fountain. Use the memorials and flags as visual landmarks before branching out across campus.
cards.short_summary: A clear opening stop for getting your bearings near central campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech identifies Memorial Circle as the focal point of campus; its flags are displayed 24 hours daily, seven days a week.
cards.source_title: Texas Tech Cuts Ribbon on Military & Veterans Tribute Walk and Wall of Honor
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; the university’s flag policy states the Memorial Circle flags are displayed 24 hours daily.

cards.title: Find Will Rogers and Soapsuds
cards.subtitle: Campus statue near Memorial Circle
cards.notes: Make this your first landmark photo, then read the base inscription and compare the statue’s direction with the university’s documented campus legend.
cards.short_summary: A documented Texas Tech landmark with a campus-specific story.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech says the Will Rogers and Soapsuds memorial was dedicated in 1950 and documents the statue’s associated campus legend.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; observe without climbing on or altering the statue.

cards.title: Use the SUB as your reset point
cards.subtitle: Campus events, services, and gathering space
cards.notes: Stop in to orient yourself to the building, check the current student-events listings, and choose a public place to regroup before continuing the loop.
cards.short_summary: A practical hub for campus services and recurring student programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech describes the Student Union Building as a place for campus events, educational opportunities, and services.
cards.access_notes: Check the SUB’s current hours and event calendar before going; programming and access can vary.

cards.title: Locate the University Library
cards.subtitle: Academic resources and library tours
cards.notes: Find the front desk and note the building for future study sessions. If a tour is offered, use it to learn where to get research and writing help.
cards.short_summary: A useful early stop for identifying academic support before classes intensify.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech’s orientation schedule lists University Library tours from the library front desk to introduce academic resources.
cards.access_notes: Library access and service hours vary; consult the current library hours page before visiting.

cards.title: Try a walk-up disc-golf round
cards.subtitle: Urbanovsky Park outdoor activity
cards.notes: Bring a disc if you have one, yield to pedestrians, and play a few holes at your own pace. It is an easy way to see part of campus outdoors.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor, self-directed activity on Texas Tech recreation grounds.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech says Urbanovsky Park has a nine-hole disc golf course and that it is for walk-up play only.
cards.access_notes: The course is walk-up play only; pedestrians have the right-of-way. Bring or arrange your own disc.

cards.entity_name: Robert H. Ewalt Student Recreation Center
cards.title: Take a self-guided Rec Center look
cards.subtitle: Recreation and fitness facilities
cards.notes: Walk through during posted operating hours to identify courts, the jogging track, and the Outdoor Pursuits Center. Confirm your eligibility before using equipment or facilities.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation stop to make future activity plans more concrete.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech states that the Robert H. Ewalt Student Recreation Center includes courts, a jogging track, fitness areas, and the Outdoor Pursuits Center.
cards.source_title: Robert H. Ewalt Student Recreation Center
cards.access_notes: Facility use is primarily for Texas Tech students, faculty, and staff; verify current hours and entry requirements before arrival.

cards.title: Spend an afternoon at the Museum
cards.subtitle: Museum of Texas Tech University
cards.notes: Choose one gallery to explore rather than rushing through everything. This is a weather-proof stop with free daily admission and free public parking.
cards.short_summary: A free museum visit with changing exhibition possibilities.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum of Texas Tech University states that admission is free every day and lists public visiting hours and free public parking.
cards.source_title: Plan your visit! | Museum | Texas Tech
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sunday noon–5 p.m.; closed Mondays and Texas Tech holidays. Hours may change.

cards.title: Walk through ranching history
cards.subtitle: National Ranching Heritage Center
cards.notes: Set aside time to walk the outdoor historic structures and exhibits. Wear comfortable shoes and check the center’s current visitor information before traveling there.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor heritage stop centered on restored ranching structures.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech describes the National Ranching Heritage Center as presenting ranching history through real ranches and heritage, and lists public hours.
cards.access_notes: The university lists public hours of 10 a.m.–5 p.m. Monday–Saturday and 1–5 p.m. Sunday; closed major holidays.

cards.title: Make a daylight trip to Lubbock Lake
cards.subtitle: TTU heritage site north of main campus
cards.notes: Plan this as a separate daytime outing: start at the interpretive center, then choose trails appropriate for the weather and your mobility needs.
cards.short_summary: A free, off-campus-adjacent heritage preserve with archaeological and natural history context.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech identifies Lubbock Lake Landmark as a 336-acre archaeological and natural-history preserve with free public admission.
cards.access_notes: Summer hours are Tuesday–Saturday 7 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sunday 1–5 p.m.; closed Mondays. Outdoor accessibility varies.

cards.title: Close with the Texas Tech Seal
cards.subtitle: Orientation photo stop
cards.notes: End the weekend with a simple photo at the seal, then save the location for when family or friends visit. Keep the stop brief and leave room for your next plan.
cards.short_summary: A documented orientation photo stop that provides a natural closing moment.
cards.evidence_claim: Texas Tech’s orientation schedule identifies the Texas Tech Seal as a stop for students to celebrate joining the Red Raider family and take photos.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor orientation stop; access is subject to campus conditions and scheduled events.
